description: ESP32 Rust firmware scaffold: minimal Cargo.toml + stable toolchain pin + src/main.rs entrypoint that compiles on stock rustup, ready to extend with esp-idf-svc for real hardware targets.

buildHints.whenToUse: Use this layer for any ESP32 Rust firmware project. It provides a compilable baseline; extend Cargo.toml with esp-idf-svc/esp-idf-hal crates and switch rust-toolchain.toml channel to 'esp' when targeting real hardware via espup.
firstSteps: Run `cargo check` to verify the baseline compiles on stable
To target real ESP32 hardware: install espup (`cargo install espup && espup install`), change rust-toolchain.toml channel to 'esp', add esp-idf-svc/esp-idf-hal to Cargo.toml
Source `$HOME/export-esp.sh` in every shell before building for hardware
Install espflash for flashing: `cargo install espflash cargo-espflash`
Flash a connected board: `cargo espflash flash --release --monitor`
gotchas: The xtensa-esp32-espidf target requires the esp-rs forked rustc. Stock stable rustup cannot resolve esp-idf-svc. Switch channel to 'esp' and run espup before adding firmware crates.
Source `$HOME/export-esp.sh` in every shell before `cargo check` or `cargo build` when using the esp channel. Without it rustc cannot find the xtensa target.
Do NOT add a build.rs unless you also add a `build` key in Cargo.toml pointing to it — a stray build.rs in the src root is silently ignored and causes confusion.
architectureNotes: The stable-channel baseline compiles as a normal Rust binary. Real ESP32 firmware replaces main() with the esp-idf-svc entrypoint pattern and pins channel = 'esp' in rust-toolchain.toml.

placeholders.description: Replace the println stub with real firmware logic using esp-idf-svc for WiFi, HTTP, and peripheral access.
Add esp-idf-svc, esp-idf-hal, anyhow, and log crates when targeting ESP32 hardware.
